transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We've got eighteen totes of spent solvent from the cleaning process staged in the waste area, and they're awaiting disposition. I know we normally send routine solvent waste to our recycling contractor, but I need to sign off on the final disposition and shipment plan before anything moves. No pickup has been booked yet, and the waste area can hold the totes in the meantime. Per policy, we need to go through the routine waste-disposition huddle first — that means hearing the compliance and logistics reports in full before I can make the disposition decision. Inventory checks and other execution details come after authorization, so they're not a blocker today. Let's get started with those reports.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical compliance issue before we proceed. My laboratory review this morning reclassified the spent solvent as UN1993 flammable liquid, packing group II — it is not routine recyclable solvent. Because of this reclassification, the 18 totes must be transferred into 18 UN-rated steel drums before shipment, and a hazardous-waste manifest is required. I have not yet entered the classification into the formal waste register because I was waiting for the plant manager's disposition signature.
